page: Google Cloud Platform h4d-standard-192 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the h4d server family. It features 192 dedicated physical cores powered by AMD EPYC 9B45 processors, with a 1.0 thread-per-core configuration. The system is equipped with 720.0 GB of RAM, providing a resource density of 3.75 GB of memory per core. The CPU cache configuration includes 48 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware, and it is provisioned with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the h4d-standard-192 demonstrates top-tier performance, placing in the top 10% across multiple categories. The dedicated AMD EPYC cores deliver a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 655,072.06 and a single-core score of 3,461.39. Memory subsystem performance is characterized by a read-only large block bandwidth of 1,054.65 GB/sec and a write large block bandwidth of 427.73 GB/sec. Database and web operations are highly efficient, with Redis SET operations reaching 495.56 million operations per second and static web serving throughput measured at 187.5 GB/sec.

The lack of local NVMe storage and GPU accelerators represents a clear architectural tradeoff, requiring external block storage for persistent data and limiting its utility for direct hardware-accelerated machine learning training. However, the high density of 192 dedicated physical cores and top-tier memory bandwidth make this instance highly cost-efficient for compute-heavy, non-GPU workloads that require massive parallel processing. Appropriate workloads include large-scale database operations, high-throughput web serving, multi-threaded decompression tasks, and intensive CPU-bound simulations.
